text:
People don’t just quit their jobs; they quit their managers. It’s a mantra we hear often, but have we ever stopped to ask, “Who’s the skip?” 

As I’ve transitioned into leadership roles, I’ve seen firsthand how the success of a manager hinges on their skip lead. The skip lead is the unsung hero, shaping the environment and expectations that allow managers to thrive. If those skip leads lack the awareness and tools to support their managers, it creates a ripple effect of disengagement and frustration that can drown even the most capable teams.

In my experience guiding product managers in AI and coaching, I’ve learned that fostering a culture of open dialogue and accountability starts at the top. So, let’s challenge ourselves to look upward and ask: “How am I supporting my managers?” 

Reflecting on the skips in your life can unlock opportunities for growth and engagement. What’s one shift you can make today to empower your team? 💡
